case.summary: Verdict: legitimate at probability 0.08 for transaction 3450629 ($100.09, online, product R, region 204.0) on card C04570-K1, pattern none, with the candidate three-member chain (3450436, 3450503, 3450629, $300.14 total in a 48-hour window) never treated as an episode since the case resolved as legitimate and exposure is $0.00. The decisive evidence spanned four families: history (the amount sits well inside the card's median-$199.97/max-$2,892.12 baseline, the region has five prior visits, and the $100.09 product-R charge to anonymous.com recurs roughly every 15 days), device (the profile is a generic, not-strong Windows/Chrome fingerprint already used on this card since October 27, so it carries no shared-origin weight despite appearing on many cards), memory (the calibrated case-memory score of 0.099 was far below the raw risk_score of 0.57, and a prior risk-score alert on this card of the same cleared_travel template, CC-1383, closed clean, echoed by same-region comparables such as CC-4955 and CC-4381 that also cleared), and customer (a validation request was sent and the simulated reply confirmed the charge). The alternative reading — that a single risk_score of 0.57 plus a proxy flag on the flagged transaction warranted treating this as unverified card-not-present fraud — was considered but rejected because it rests on one weak signal against three independent legitimacy families. Nothing further needs approval beyond the auto-route actions already taken: CREATE_CASE, ALLOW_TRANSACTION, and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, all executable by the agent with no L1/L2 escalation required.
